SPIRALION.specialization: cumulative reasoning checkpoint continuity and contradiction management
tasks: A verified checkpoint contains a finished proof step and one explicit residual. The next response should resume from that residual without rebuilding prior sections.
Two new receipts make mutually incompatible claims while the prior checkpoint remains valid.
A session has forty verified notes with repeated statements and must be reduced to a compact state preserving proofs, unknowns and dependencies.
A continuation depends on one unverified external constant before any new deduction can be trusted.
A long research chain has a stable checkpoint and a newly assigned subproblem directly downstream of it.
One artifact says PASS and another says FAIL for the same pinned input and code revision.
Five near-duplicate summaries contain the same result and should become one nonredundant checkpoint.
A claimed improvement has no cold-test receipt yet, so the immediate next action is evidence acquisition.
The exact previous residual is known and no new conflict or missing dependency has appeared.
A newly produced conclusion conflicts with a previously verified invariant.
A memory packet exceeds context budget but its verified facts, failures and open questions must survive.
A simulation result is present but the mission requires deciding whether it transfers to a physical claim.

HYPERION.specialization: divergent hypotheses alternative mechanisms and counterfactual search
tasks: A dominant explanation exists, but the task asks for a distinct plausible explanation compatible with the same observation.
The task asks what would change if one key assumption were reversed while all other conditions stayed fixed.
Several correlations are known and the next objective is to propose a causal process that could generate them.
Five candidate solutions are minor variants of the same method and the search needs genuinely different approaches.
A proposed architecture has one known design path and the mission requests another architecture with different tradeoffs.
The question asks whether the conclusion still holds if gravity is absent from the model.
Observed instability needs a physically interpretable chain of causes rather than another numerical fit.
A brainstorming set has converged prematurely on one representation and needs orthogonal representations.
A theorem attempt fails on one lemma and the task asks for a different proof route.
The experiment succeeded; now assess the hypothetical case where the control variable had been held constant.
A component overheats repeatedly and the goal is a causal failure mechanism explaining the pattern.
Multiple agents copied the same idea; the next action is to generate non-overlapping candidate families.

ASTRION.specialization: aerospace R&D systems physics trajectory propulsion and validation
tasks: A spacecraft concept has no frozen payload mass, mission delta-v or lifetime target.
Mission requirements are frozen, but thermal and propulsion interactions have not yet been represented mathematically.
A validated rocket-equation model and all inputs are available; the needed output is propellant mass.
A thruster design is numerically promising and now needs a controlled hot-fire experiment with acceptance criteria.
A lunar cargo vehicle proposal lacks landing accuracy and payload throughput requirements.
A reentry concept has geometry and boundary conditions but no aerodynamic heating model.
Orbital radii and gravitational parameter are fixed for a Hohmann transfer computation.
A structural simulation passes but the mission requires validating the joint under representative load.
A space tug concept has no defined duty cycle, refueling interval or target orbit class.
A cryogenic tank system needs a boil-off and heat-leak model before sizing insulation.
A nozzle model, chamber conditions and gas properties are fixed; compute the performance metric.
A guidance algorithm works in simulation and needs hardware-in-the-loop validation before operational claims.

SAPHEA_MICRO.specialization: routing compact specialist selection and minimal useful coalition
tasks: A new task arrives and must first be assigned to the smallest useful specialist set.
The task is proving an algebraic identity with no need for web research or code execution.
A failing Python test has a traceback and the next step is debugging the implementation.
A claim depends on a current external paper and its provenance must be retrieved.
The goal is generating a novel mechanical architecture under explicit constraints.
A proposed result looks plausible but needs active search for counterexamples and hidden assumptions.
Several specialist outputs are available and must be merged without counting correlated evidence twice.
A mixed request contains math, code and research, and orchestration must select only the necessary modules.
A finite combinatorial recurrence requires symbolic derivation rather than implementation work.
The requested work is to implement and test a deterministic parser.
A product specification may have changed recently and must be verified from sources.
The task asks for multiple radically different propulsion concepts before evaluation.
A benchmark gain may be leakage and the mission is to falsify that explanation.
Independent and correlated findings must be synthesized into one evidence-weighted decision.
